name: LangGraph

choose_when: Teams want one Python ML workflow across local development and interchangeable production stacks.
avoid_when: A single established orchestrator already covers the lifecycle with less abstraction.
failure_mode: An abstraction layer cannot make incompatible backend semantics identical; cache and artifact behavior must be verified per stack.
quickstart:
pip install zenml
zenml init
mental_model: Think of ZenML as a mlops pipeline framework between python steps + stack and versioned artifacts and run; its defining mechanism is portable ml pipeline.

architecture.label: Control plane
architecture.detail: Events or schedules materialize a versioned task or asset graph with retries, backfills, lineage, validation, and promotion gates.

architecture.label: State and trust boundary
architecture.detail: Source snapshots, schemas, code, environments, artifacts, partitions, run ids, lineage, quality results, and approvals must be replayable.

tutorial.title: 1. Problem and abstraction
tutorial.body: Portable steps and pipelines connected to artifact stores, orchestrators, experiment trackers, deployers, and infrastructure stacks. Think of ZenML as a mlops pipeline framework between python steps + stack and versioned artifacts and run; its defining mechanism is portable ml pipeline.

tutorial.title: 2. Structure and execution
tutorial.body: Follow the data path Python steps + stack → Portable ML pipeline → Versioned artifacts and run. Events or schedules materialize a versioned task or asset graph with retries, backfills, lineage, validation, and promotion gates.

tutorial.title: 3. State, security, and operations
tutorial.body: Source snapshots, schemas, code, environments, artifacts, partitions, run ids, lineage, quality results, and approvals must be replayable.

tutorial.title: 4. Selection decision
tutorial.body: Choose it when teams want one Python ML workflow across local development and interchangeable production stacks. Reject it when a single established orchestrator already covers the lifecycle with less abstraction. Compare the same representative workload with Metaflow, Kubeflow Pipelines, Flyte.

tutorial.title: 5. Production proof
tutorial.body: Start with the failure hypothesis: An abstraction layer cannot make incompatible backend semantics identical; cache and artifact behavior must be verified per stack. Backfill at scale, kill workers mid-effect, change schemas, restore artifacts, reproduce a release, and reconcile every ambiguous outcome.

name: Zep
summary: Temporal knowledge and conversation memory designed to assemble relevant user and agent context over time.
choose_when: Agents need durable, evolving user or entity context with retrieval and provenance beyond a short chat buffer.
avoid_when: Simple session history, explicit relational facts, or application-owned event sourcing is sufficient.
failure_mode: Automatically extracted memories can become stale, cross tenant boundaries, or be treated as authority without provenance and correction.

pip install zep-cloud
from zep_cloud.client import Zep
mental_model: Think of Zep as a agent memory and context platform between conversation events and context for the next turn; its defining mechanism is temporal memory graph.

tutorial.title: 1. Problem and abstraction
tutorial.body: Python framework for steps, artifacts, versions, retries, cards, parallelism, and moving data-science workflows to cloud compute. Think of Metaflow as a human-friendly data science workflow framework between python flow + data and run artifacts + cards; its defining mechanism is versioned steps on local or cloud compute.

tutorial.title: 2. Structure and execution
tutorial.body: Follow the data path Python flow + data → Versioned steps on local or cloud compute → Run artifacts + cards. Events or schedules materialize a versioned task or asset graph with retries, backfills, lineage, validation, and promotion gates.

tutorial.title: 3. State, security, and operations
tutorial.body: Source snapshots, schemas, code, environments, artifacts, partitions, run ids, lineage, quality results, and approvals must be replayable.

tutorial.title: 4. Selection decision
tutorial.body: Choose it when data scientists need a gentle local-to-cloud path with inspectable run artifacts and step semantics. Reject it when a Kubernetes-native platform or asset-centric data orchestration is the organization standard. Compare the same representative workload with Flyte, Prefect, Dagster.

tutorial.title: 5. Production proof
tutorial.body: Start with the failure hypothesis: Implicit artifact capture and environment differences can create large state, slow resumes, or non-reproducible cloud runs. Backfill at scale, kill workers mid-effect, change schemas, restore artifacts, reproduce a release, and reconcile every ambiguous outcome.
